Cross-checked _design-system/REMOVED.md and TASTE_LOG.md for motion/animation/haptic entries (2 REMOVED hits, both about a specific staff-avatar wave and a filter-chip check, neither overlapping any finding below). Then verified every candidate against live code: app/globals.css (.salon-card-stagger keyframe block), app/[locale]/_components/search/SearchTemplate.tsx (PAGE_SIZE + stagger class usage), app/[locale]/_components/primitives/motion.ts (ENTER_RECIPE, useStepSwapMotion, full source read), components-legacy/booking/BookingWizard.tsx (real step-swap call site, full source read), tailwind.config.js (transitionProperty groups), package.json (check:motion/gate:motion scripts), .claude/settings.json and .github/ (grepped for gate wiring, both empty), a repo-wide grep for AnimatePresence mode=, framer-motion type:"spring" call sites, and solen-mobile/_design-system/THEMING.md's own haptics self-audit. Absence proofs below list the exact grep patterns run over _design-system, _rules, _docs, CLAUDE.md and ~/.claude. This domain already has one of the most rigorous research files in the whole estate (TASTE_MOTION.md explicitly separates T1/T2/T3/CONV evidence tiers and names 14 things the research does NOT support), so most easy gaps are already closed; the 9 findings below are the ones that survived that bar, several caught only by reading the actual .ts/.tsx source rather than the docs describing it.

findings.title: Interruptibility is a stated rule with no technical contract, and the default framer-motion pattern used on the highest-traffic surface violates it
findings.principle: Any AnimatePresence wrapping a step-swap, tab-swap, or other frequently-retriggered transition must use mode="popLayout" (or unmounted-immediately exits), never mode="wait". A user acting again mid-transition must see the new content start entering immediately; the outgoing content is allowed to keep exiting underneath it, but it may never gate the incoming content's start. Grep the codebase for AnimatePresence mode="wait" on every PR touching app/**/*.tsx and components*/**/*.tsx; a new instance on a surface a user can retrigger (not a one-shot modal) is a defect, not a style choice.
findings.why: MOTION.md's THE SPEED LAW hard rule 4 says 'Interruptible. A user acting again mid-motion must not be made to wait for the first one to finish,' and TASTE_MOTION.md finding 18 spends a full section arguing this is the real lever behind 'our product feels static,' bigger than the duration number. But neither document ever says what 'interruptible' means in framer-motion terms. Framer Motion's own AnimatePresence mode="wait" does the literal opposite: it holds the entering child off the DOM until the exiting child's exit animation fully finishes. A rule that says 'must not be made to wait' with no implementation contract is unenforceable, and the codebase proves it: mode="wait" is the dominant pattern, not the exception.
findings.local_evidence: grep -rn 'AnimatePresence' app --include=*.tsx | grep -i 'mode=' returns 9 hits, all mode="wait": auth/register/page.tsx:299, _components/homepage/SearchBar.tsx:429, _components/homepage/BentoBusiness.tsx:410, _components/search/SearchOverlay.tsx:793 and :865, _components/search/SearchTemplate.tsx:1929, dev/map-motion/page.tsx:205, onboarding/salon/page.tsx:666, dev/search-morph/page.tsx:372. Confirmed live in production code by reading components-legacy/booking/BookingWizard.tsx:213-225 directly: the step content (services -> staff -> datetime -> hair -> pay-confirm, the single flow that converts revenue) is wrapped in `<AnimatePresence mode="wait" custom={1}>` around `variants={stepSwapVariants}` from the shared `useStepSwapMotion()` primitive (motion.ts:166). This is the exact surface TASTE_MOTION finding 18 and LOCKFILE SS16.5 were written to protect, and it is the one place a user is most likely to tap Next twice.

findings.title: THE CURVE RULE's own audit missed the shared step-swap primitive: it exits on the entrance curve, not the exit curve
findings.principle: Every AnimatePresence exit transition must use the accelerate curve (`thud`, cubic-bezier(0.7,0,0.84,0)), never the decelerate curve (`glide`) it entered on. When an enter/exit pair is built as a single shared transition object (one `Transition` reused for both `animate` and `exit`), that reuse is itself the defect: split enter and exit into two transitions with two different eases, even when the other numbers (duration, scale delta) stay identical.
findings.why: MOTION.md's own THE CURVE RULE (added 2026-07-25, D4 in MOTION_LAW.md) states the assignment explicitly: entering = `glide` decelerate, exiting = `thud` accelerate, and it names four call sites it repointed (Sheet, Modal, Sheet-backdrop on `snap`; Toast on `glide`). It missed a fifth, and it is the highest-traffic one: `useStepSwapMotion` in app/[locale]/_components/primitives/motion.ts is the shared step-swap primitive, and BookingWizard.tsx (the booking flow every paying customer goes through) is its real call site. A rule that ships with a fix list and misses its own most-used primitive means the audit method (grep for named tokens) did not catch a primitive that reuses one Transition object for both directions.
findings.local_evidence: app/[locale]/_components/primitives/motion.ts:166-181 (useStepSwapMotion): `const stepSwapTransition: Transition = { duration: STEP_SWAP_DURATION, ease: GLIDE_EASE };` is declared once (line 138) and reused for both `animate` (center) and `exit` (return statement, line 178-179: `transition: stepSwapTransition` applied uniformly across the whole Variants object). components-legacy/booking/BookingWizard.tsx:213-225 confirms the real call site: `const { variants: stepSwapVariants, transition: stepSwapTransition } = useStepSwapMotion();` then `<AnimatePresence mode="wait" custom={1}><motion.div variants={stepSwapVariants} initial="enter" animate="center" exit="exit" transition={stepSwapTransition}>`. Every booking step that slides out is decelerating on the way out, the exact 'visibly slows down leaving' defect MOTION.md itself uses to describe the Toast bug it already fixed.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n 'thud' app/[locale]/_components/primitives/motion.ts -> zero hits; the file that defines the app's single most-reused enter/exit primitive never imports or references the accelerate curve at all. grep -n 'stepSwapVariants\|stepSwapTransition\|useStepSwapMotion' _design-system/MOTION.md _plans/MOTION_LAW.md -> zero hits; THE CURVE RULE's own fix list (MOTION.md, 'THE CURVE RULE' section) names Sheet/Modal/sheet-backdrop/Toast by name and does not mention step-swap at all.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: THE CURVE RULE (MOTION.md) states the correct general principle and has already fixed 4 of what should have been at least 5 sites; the delta is this fifth site, plus the more durable fix (split shared Transition objects that serve both directions, which is what let the first four bugs and this one happen the same way).
findings.where_it_should_live: app/[locale]/_components/primitives/motion.ts (code fix: separate enterTransition/exitTransition inside useStepSwapMotion) + _design-system/MOTION.md THE CURVE RULE section (name the fifth site so the audit record is honest)
findings.enforcement: checklist item for the D4 repoint work already queued in MOTION_LAW.md, plus a check-motion.mjs rule that flags any Variants object whose exit state cites the same transition reference as its animate/visible state

findings.title: The stagger recipe has no ceiling: past 8 items, new cards enter at the same instant as the first card, on the app's own largest feed
findings.principle: Every stagger container must define a hard ceiling (a maximum stagger-eligible index, e.g. 8) AND an explicit overflow rule for items beyond it: either (a) cap all items beyond the ceiling at the LAST defined delay (so item 9+ enters together with item 8, never with item 1), or (b) disable per-item stagger entirely past the ceiling and let the remainder enter as one group at the ceiling's delay. A stagger utility that silently falls back to a delay of 0 for unenumerated children is a defect, because 0 means 'enters with the very first item,' the opposite of graceful degradation.
findings.why: A cascading entrance is legible because each item's delay is monotonically later than the one before it. When the CSS only enumerates delays for a fixed number of children and every unenumerated child inherits the undeclared default (0ms, same as the FIRST child), items beyond the ceiling do not degrade to 'no stagger', they degrade to 'wrong stagger': they appear to jump the queue and enter alongside item 1, ahead of items 2 through 8. On a results grid this reads as visual noise or a rendering glitch, the exact 'raggedy' quality the ENTER RECIPE was built to eliminate for single-element entrances.
findings.local_evidence: app/globals.css:526-538: `.salon-card-stagger > *` sets the shared keyframe animation with no delay, then `:nth-child(1)` through `:nth-child(8)` override animation-delay from 0ms to 350ms in 50ms steps; there is no rule for :nth-child(9) or beyond, so those children keep the base rule's implicit animation-delay: 0ms (browser default), identical to :nth-child(1). app/[locale]/_components/search/SearchTemplate.tsx:140 sets `const PAGE_SIZE = 12;` and line 1616 applies the `salon-card-stagger` class to the results grid that renders up to PAGE_SIZE items per page. So on the single feed in the app most likely to render more than 8 items at once (search results), cards 9 through 12 enter at t=0, simultaneously with card 1, ahead of cards 2-8.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn 'stagger' _design-system/MOTION.md _design-system/LOCKFILE.md _design-system/research/TASTE_MOTION.md _design-system/RATIONALE.md -> hits are all about WHAT stagger delay to use (40ms/50ms, MOTION.md motion-22 table row 'List first-load | stagger rise-in') never about a ceiling or overflow behavior. grep -rn 'nth-child(8)\|stagger.*ceiling\|stagger.*cap\|stagger.*overflow\|stagger.*limit' _design-system -> zero hits anywhere in the design law.
findings.existing_coverage: none: the motion-22 vocabulary table (MOTION.md) and RATIONALE.md both specify the per-item delay value (40-50ms) but never address what happens once the container has more children than the CSS enumerates delays for.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/MOTION.md (motion-22 vocabulary table, 'List first-load' row) + app/globals.css (code fix: an nth-child(n+9) rule matching the last defined delay, or a JS-driven stagger with a computed min(index, 8))
findings.enforcement: gate: scripts/check-motion.mjs (already a runtime probe) extended to flag any CSS stagger selector whose enumerated nth-child range is smaller than a real page's rendered item count for the class it targets

findings.title: The one runtime WCAG 2.2.2 check the estate built for itself is a manual command, not a gate
findings.principle: A runtime check that exists to catch an accessibility Level-A violation (auto-starting motion running past 5 seconds beside other content) must run automatically on every change that can introduce one: a pre-commit hook, a CI job, or both. A script sitting in package.json that nobody is forced to invoke is not enforcement, it is documentation of what enforcement would look like.
findings.why: TASTE_MOTION.md finding 14 identifies WCAG SC 2.2.2 (Level A, not the aspirational AAA one) as the system's actual exposure, and MOTION_LAW.md's own D2 box describes discovering 8 automatic animate-spin sites and 25 automatic animate-pulse sites that a purely static, by-hand audit had already missed or miscounted six-fold, which is exactly why check-motion.mjs was built to probe at runtime instead of scanning class names. Having built the right tool, leaving it unwired means the next new shimmer, ping, or breathe utility added to globals.css or a new component gets zero automatic scrutiny, and the estate already has direct proof (the D2 undercount) that this specific defect class hides from anything less than a runtime probe.
findings.local_evidence: package.json:17-19 defines `check:motion`, `check:motion:slow`, and `gate:motion` (`node scripts/check-motion.mjs --gate`) as npm scripts. grep -rln 'check-motion\|check:motion\|gate:motion' .claude/hooks (both the project's and ~/.claude/hooks) returns zero hits. grep -n 'check-motion\|check:motion\|motion' /Users/sulo/.claude/settings.json returns only motion-recipe-gate.py (which checks the ENTER RECIPE's opacity+scale+blur triad on new code, an unrelated concern from the WCAG loop check). grep -n 'check-motion\|check:motion' .github/**/*.yml returns zero hits; no CI workflow calls it either.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn 'gate.*motion\|motion.*gate\|wcag.*2\.2\.2\|pause.*stop.*hide' _rules CLAUDE.md .claude/hooks -> only the already-cited TASTE_MOTION.md and MOTION_LAW.md hits; no _rules file or hook config references check-motion.mjs at all outside the design-system research docs describing what it does.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the check itself exists and is proven to work (MOTION_LAW.md D2: 'proven both directions on real cases... its own self-test found a bug in it'), the missing piece is purely the wiring, which the estate's own reference_gate_wiring_sandbox_block memory note names as a recurring failure mode (a gate built in a sandboxed session is not armed because settings.json is unwritable there).
findings.where_it_should_live: package.json (add to a pre-commit or lint-staged step) + .github/workflows (add a CI job) + ~/.claude/settings.json if a PreToolUse hook variant is wanted for local dev too

findings.title: iOS haptics has no locked action-to-tier vocabulary; the mobile design system records this as an open, unresolved split
findings.principle: Every action class (selection, confirmation of a reversible save, a destructive action, a success peak, an error, a drag-boundary hit) maps to exactly one of the haptic wrapper's named tiers, in one canonical table (the mobile equivalent of MOTION.md's motion-22 table), and every call site imports that single wrapper. A component that calls `expo-haptics` (or its native equivalent) directly, bypassing the shared wrapper, is drift the same way a hand-rolled framer-motion entrance bypassing useEnterMotion is drift on web.
findings.why: Haptics is explicitly named in this domain's scope ('haptics on iOS'), and unlike web motion (which has the fully-specified motion-22 table), the mobile app has never converged on one. Without a locked table, two developers building adjacent features independently guess which of the 6 tiers (select/light/medium/success/warning/error) fits a given action, and the two 2026-07-12-counted populations (24 files on the wrapper vs 19 calling the native API directly) show that guessing is already happening at scale, roughly evenly split, with no owner decision forcing convergence.

COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md's haptics line (selectionAsync on pickers/chips, impactLight on heart-save, notificationSuccess on booking confirm) documents 3 of the wrapper's 6 tiers, not the full vocabulary.' package.json:18 in solen-mobile confirms expo-haptics ~15.0.8 is an active dependency, and grep -rln 'Haptics\|expo-haptics' solen-mobile --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx (excluding node_modules) returns 20 files, corroborating the split THEMING.md counted.

findings.title: LOCKFILE still tells engineers box-shadow is compositor-friendly to animate, contradicted by the estate's own sourced research, and a reachable transition group still offers it
findings.principle: The compositor-safe animatable-property list must read 'transform, opacity, and filter only' and must explicitly say box-shadow is EXCLUDED because it triggers a repaint every frame, not merely omit it by silence. Any shared transition-property utility (Tailwind's transitionProperty config or equivalent) that bundles box-shadow with transform under a name implying both are cheap must either be removed or renamed so it cannot be reached for by a developer skimming utility names for 'the hover-lift one'.
findings.why: TASTE_MOTION.md finding 25 already did the work: it cites web.dev's paint-cost documentation verbatim ('drawing a drop-shadow on a DOM element involves a multi-pass operation with splines... as opposed to opacity which should be easier to render') and recommends the fix (animate a pre-rendered shadow layer's opacity plus a translateY transform, never box-shadow itself). But the law it should have corrected was never touched: LOCKFILE SS3.5 still says the opposite in the same design system, and a utility group that packages the disproved pattern under a plausible name is exactly the kind of trap a developer reaches for without re-deriving the research, which is the entire reason a LOCKFILE exists.
findings.local_evidence: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md:569 (read directly): 'Animate `transform` + `box-shadow` only (compositor-friendly). Honor SS4 anti-patterns (no will-change at rest; gate backdrop-blur on scroll containers).' tailwind.config.js:331-334 (read directly): `transitionProperty: { ..., "shadow-transform": "box-shadow, transform", "colors-shadow": "color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow", ... }`. grep -rn 'shadow-transform' app (excluding node_modules) returns zero live class-name usages today, so the trap is dormant, not yet biting a real surface, which is why this is medium and not high.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n 'box-shadow' _design-system/research/TASTE_MOTION.md -> finding 25 and its mapping-table row 25 are the correction; grep -n 'box-shadow' _design-system/LOCKFILE.md -> line 569 (the uncorrected claim) and line 605 ('Anti-patterns (NEVER)' list, which never mentions box-shadow at all, only will-change and backdrop-filter). No line in LOCKFILE.md was edited after TASTE_MOTION.md finding 25 was written; the mapping table's own row 25 recommendation ('Stop transitioning box-shadow on hover-heavy surfaces') was never applied back to the law it corrects.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the correct finding already exists, sourced, in TASTE_MOTION.md finding 25 and its mapping row; the delta is that the correction was never propagated to the actual locked rule (LOCKFILE SS3.5) or to the tailwind config that operationalizes the wrong version.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md SS3.5 line 569 (edit the sentence) + tailwind.config.js (rename or split the shadow-transform group)
findings.enforcement: checklist item, or extend the existing drift-checker (solen-drift-check) with a rule flagging any `transition-shadow-transform` class usage or raw `transition: box-shadow` in new code

findings.title: Physics-spring parameters have no locked house values outside the one gesture-release formula, so the word "spring" resolves to two unrelated mechanisms depending on the file
findings.principle: Every non-gesture framer-motion `type: "spring"` call site must draw its stiffness/damping (or response/dampingFraction) pair from a small named, locked set (e.g. `SPRING_GENTLE`, `SPRING_SNAPPY`, `SPRING_BOUNCY`, mirroring SwiftUI's own named presets that TASTE_MOTION finding 18 already holds up as the vocabulary worth copying), exported from the same primitives module as ENTER_RECIPE. The CSS easing token also named "spring" (a bezier approximation used for in-place color/toggle flips) must be renamed or clearly scoped in its own doc comment as a DIFFERENT mechanism from a physics spring, so a developer reading `ease-spring` in one file and `type:"spring", stiffness: 200` in another does not assume they are the same thing tuned two ways.
findings.why: LOCKFILE SS16.5.4 proves the house already knows how to lock spring house values correctly, for exactly one use case (gesture release). Everywhere else, six-plus call sites hand-pick stiffness and damping per file with no shared constant, meaning every 'bouncy reveal' in the app has a visibly different bounce, spend, and settle time by accident of who wrote that file, not by design intent, the same inconsistency the ENTER RECIPE was built to kill for opacity/scale/blur entrances. The naming collision compounds it: LOCKFILE SS4 defines 'spring' as a fixed CSS cubic-bezier curve for in-place flips (toggle, check), a completely different animation model (deterministic, no velocity, no interruption) from the physics springs used elsewhere, so the one word means two things depending on whether you are in tailwind.config.js or a .tsx file.
findings.local_evidence: grep -rn 'type: "spring"\|stiffness\|damping' app --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx (excluding node_modules) surfaces at least 6 distinct hand-picked pairs: HeroDuo.tsx:92 (stiffness:110, damping:18), HeroDuo.tsx:113-114 (stiffness:120, damping:18, mass:0.6), HeroDuo.tsx:138 (stiffness:200, damping:22), BentoCard.tsx:50-55 (damping:30, stiffness:200), BentoBusiness.tsx:495 (bounce:0.05, duration:0.4, a THIRD parameterization style), TipSheet.tsx:46 (damping:34, stiffness:340), dev/map-zoom/page.tsx:46 and :58 (stiffness:280/damping:18 and stiffness:420/damping:16 in the SAME file for two different elements). tailwind.config.js:327 defines the CSS token: `"spring": "cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)", // bouncy reveal (toggle, check)`, a fixed bezier curve, contradicting the physics-spring model used everywhere above. _plans/TASTE_RATIONALE.md:12,55 and _plans/WORKLOG.md:101 already name this exact collision ('spring double-definition (bezier vs physics)') as a PARKED, unresolved finding from an earlier audit pass.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n 'spring' _design-system/QUESTIONS.md -> zero hits; the parked finding was never promoted to a QUESTIONS.md entry, so it has no owner-facing question and no resolution date. grep -rn 'spring.*house\|spring.*preset\|SPRING_GENTLE\|SPRING_SNAPPY\|SPRING_BOUNCY' _design-system app -> zero hits anywhere; no such locked set exists outside SS16.5.4's gesture-specific formula.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: LOCKFILE SS16.5.4 proves the pattern (locked stiffness/damping constants) works and is already law for ONE case; TASTE_RATIONALE.md already flagged the naming collision as parked. The delta is extending the SAME locking discipline to non-gesture celebratory/decorative springs, and actually resolving (not just parking) the naming collision.
findings.where_it_should_live: app/[locale]/_components/primitives/motion.ts (export the locked spring presets alongside ENTER_RECIPE) + _design-system/LOCKFILE.md SS4 (rename the CSS bezier token or add a disambiguating note)
findings.enforcement: gate: extend motion-recipe-gate.py to flag a net-new `type: "spring"` framer-motion transition with inline stiffness/damping literals not imported from the primitives module

findings.title: No contract for animating a list that reorders under the user without an error or a full refetch
findings.principle: When an already-rendered list's item ORDER changes while the surface is visible and no error/refetch cycle is involved (a live queue position update, a re-sort after a background price/availability change, a realtime rank change), the transition must preserve each item's visual continuity: measure its old position, let it animate (transform-only) to its new position over the snap tier (150ms), and never unmount/remount the row or silently teleport it. This is a distinct case from Pattern 5 (stale/refreshing, where the whole surface's DATA is stale) and from the realtime-mismatch error branch (a toast plus a 3-second auto-refresh); reordering the same, still-valid data is neither an error nor staleness, and treating it as one produces an unnecessary toast or a jarring full redraw for a normal, expected event.
findings.why: Solen already has at least one live, real-time-driven ranked list (the walk-in queue tracker) and multiple sortable browse surfaces where the ranking can legitimately change while a user is looking (a filter narrowing results, a live availability drop). The motion-22 vocabulary table has an entry for a NUMBER changing in place ('Live position/number updates -> departure-board flip .animate-num-flip'), which covers the digit inside one row updating, but nothing covers the DOM position of that row changing relative to its siblings, which is a different animation problem (a FLIP-style transform, not a text-flip). Left unspecified, the two plausible default behaviors, a silent instant reflow or a full list re-render, are both worse than a position-preserving transition: one produces the 'items silently teleport' bug, the other looks like data loss.
findings.local_evidence: _design-system/components/LoadingStates.md Pattern 5 (lines 227-243, read in full): covers only the case where the SAME items stay in place and the surface indicates a background refetch (thin progress bar, old data stays at 100% opacity); its anti-pattern list explicitly forbids replacing rendered data with skeletons, but says nothing about a rank change. LoadingStates.md's error-source table (line 159) has one row for 'Realtime sync mismatch: Toast + auto-refresh after 3s', which is a CONFLICT-resolution path (something is now wrong), not a graceful in-place reorder. MOTION.md's motion-22 table (line 114) has 'Live position/number updates | departure-board flip | .animate-num-flip', confirmed by grep to key on a single number's value, not on a DOM-order swap between rows.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rni 'reorder\|re-order\|FLIP\b\|position change\|realtime.*reorder\|sort.*chang' _design-system _rules -> hits are all about drag-to-reorder ADMIN tooling (dashboard services list, discovery-admin image order, both internal, both user-INITIATED drags with index-snap, not data-driven reordering) or unrelated feature-flag 'flip' usages (V3-promotion flag flip, calendar-flip fixes). None address a list item's RANK changing due to external data, only user-dragged reordering.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: Pattern 5 (staleness) and the realtime-mismatch error row are adjacent but address different triggers (staleness, conflict) than a legitimate live rank change with no error and no staleness.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/components/LoadingStates.md (new Pattern 6: 'Live reorder') + MOTION.md motion-22 table (a new row distinct from 'Live position/number updates')

findings.title: Motion complexity never degrades for device capability, only for explicit user opt-in
findings.principle: On top of `prefers-reduced-motion` (a user's explicit request), the app should read at least one coarse, cheap device-capability signal (`navigator.hardwareConcurrency`, `navigator.deviceMemory`, or `navigator.connection.saveData`/`effectiveType`) once per session and, below a named threshold, drop the expensive tier of the motion stack (blur filters on entrance, simultaneous stagger, non-essential spring physics) while KEEPING the cheap tier (opacity/transform press feedback, the snap-tier state flips). This is a distinct control from prefers-reduced-motion: a capable device with an unbothered user should keep the full recipe; a genuinely low-end device should get a lighter recipe even if the user never touched an accessibility setting.
findings.why: THE SPEED LAW and THE ENTER RECIPE were captured and tuned against an iPhone UA in a Playwright 390x844 viewport, a mid-to-high-end reference device; the marketplace's own positioning (mid-market, price-sensitive Swiss salons and their customers) does not guarantee that device class on the customer side, and a blur filter plus a scale transform plus opacity, animated across a 12-item stagger, is real compositor and paint work that a low-end Android handles measurably worse than the capture device. Without a capability-based fallback, the ONLY lever a struggling device has is the same one a user with vestibular sensitivity has (prefers-reduced-motion), which conflates two unrelated needs and requires a user to know a system setting exists rather than the app adapting on its own.
findings.local_evidence: grep -c 'prefers-reduced-motion' app/globals.css -> 11 occurrences, confirming reduced-motion IS wired broadly. grep -rln 'hardwareConcurrency\|navigator.connection\|deviceMemory\|effectiveType' app lib (excluding node_modules) -> zero hits anywhere in the codebase; no capability-based branch exists at all, in any file, for any surface.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rni 'low-end\|low end device\|device.*perf\|frame budget\|60fps\|jank\|dropped frame\|cpu throttl' _design-system/MOTION.md _design-system/research/TASTE_MOTION.md _design-system/LOCKFILE.md -> zero hits; TASTE_MOTION.md's own finding 8 discusses attention cost of looping animation and finding 25 discusses paint cost of box-shadow, but neither proposes a device-capability check, only a property-choice fix. No file in _design-system mentions hardwareConcurrency, deviceMemory, or connection.effectiveType.
findings.existing_coverage: none: prefers-reduced-motion is the only motion-scaling lever documented or built anywhere in the estate; there is no capability-based tier at all.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/MOTION.md (new section, sibling to THE SPEED LAW) + a shared hook alongside useReducedMotion in app/[locale]/_components/primitives/motion.ts
findings.enforcement: behavioral rule for now (no existing gate could check for a missing capability branch); candidate for a future design-verifier check once a reference implementation exists
